nodes.label: Face attendance safeguards
nodes.rationale: How face data is stored, who may be enrolled, how a device's recognitions are checked before they become attendance, and how a device is tied to the lecture the teacher opened.

nodes.label: Face templates
nodes.rationale: Recognition runs on the device. The server stores one 192-float template per person and pushes it to devices. The server never receives camera frames for recognition; it receives the device's verdict: confidence and optionally liveness score and frame hash.

nodes.label: Face template encryption
nodes.rationale: Templates are encrypted with Fernet under FACE_TEMPLATE_KEY. The key lives in the environment, never in the database or the repository, so a database dump alone does not expose biometric data. Reads accept legacy plaintext; writes always encrypt when a key is set. Do not run production without a key. /health reports the key as configured or missing but does not return 503, because an installation without face attendance has no key. Rotation uses FACE_TEMPLATE_KEY_PREVIOUS and flask face rotate-key for every tenant.

nodes.label: Face consent
nodes.rationale: face_consents holds one row per person per notice version. With FACE_CONSENT_REQUIRED, the default, registration, template upload, distribution and recognition all need an active consent for the current notice version. Withdrawal deletes templates at once and is audited. Raising the notice version makes everyone re-consent; old rows stay as history but no longer count.

nodes.label: Face template retention
nodes.rationale: The nightly close-day job and flask face purge delete templates after FACE_RETENTION_DAYS when every consent is withdrawn, the user has been inactive, or consent is required and was never given. Withdrawal already deletes immediately; the purge catches older rows. Attendance rows and the recognition audit are kept; only the biometric template goes.

nodes.label: Passive liveness and recognition audit
nodes.rationale: A device cannot be fully trusted: a photo held up to the camera will match. Every Present or Late sync event is checked and one face_recognition_audit row is written. Rejection reasons are low confidence below 0.70, low liveness below 0.50 when a score was sent, a duplicate frame hash within 600 seconds, a template older than 730 days, or no consent. A rejected event is not written to attendance_logs. Manual marks and Absent skip the checks. Devices without a liveness model are accepted on confidence alone, so models that produce a score are preferred.

nodes.label: Lecture session codes
nodes.rationale: lecture_sessions.session_code from revision 0007 is now used so a device marks only the lecture the teacher opened. Opening a lecture records it as held and issues an 8-character code valid for 90 minutes. Only the device owner's lectures can be opened from that device. FACE_REQUIRE_SESSION_CODE defaults to false so a college can roll devices out before switching the requirement on. When the flag is off, a code is checked only when one is sent.
